run: NeuroAxis v19 — comprehensive all-dimension audit: features, facts, rendering, UX, robustness, code quality
scope: Accessibility (WCAG 2.1), discoverability, feedback, layout/consistency and naming/UX-writing of the shipped interface. Findings only — no product or data file was edited. Every finding names a file:line, a selector or a data id. Contrast ratios were computed from the hex values in src/styles/tokens.css against the surfaces the CSS actually paints, with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula (sRGB, 0.04045 knee). No browser was available in this sandbox: every consequence that would need a screenshot or an accessibility-tree dump is labelled as such, and a claim that depends on assistive-technology behaviour is verdict 'unverifiable-here' rather than 'wrong'.

findings.subject: Live-section canvas wrapper — the AX atom that swallows its own controls (SectionCanvas.tsx:2380-2611)
findings.field: div.section-canvas-wrap[role="img"][aria-label="Live 2D {axis} synced to the clip slider"] (src/components/section/SectionCanvas.tsx:2383-2384)
findings.claimed: The file states (SectionCanvas.tsx:2356-2363) that the wrapper "is a single role=\"img\" with a fixed aria-label and no text", and that the structure chip "is the ONE accessible instance of a structure name this component owns". Because the wrapper is an AX atom, that sentence describes the opposite of the outcome.
findings.expected: A wrapper that CONTAINS interactive controls and a live status label must not carry a children-presentational role. Either the wrapper is a named role="group" (the fix this repo already applied to the plate root for exactly this defect class) or the four DOM children must be re-parented outside it.
findings.basis: WAI-ARIA 1.2 lists role="img" with `children presentational: true` — its subtree contributes NO nodes to the accessibility tree. The four children that disappear: button.section-lobes-toggle (the cortical-divisions layer switch, SectionCanvas.tsx:2507-2525), button.section-plate-chip ("≈ <level> (<d> au) — open", :2585-2601), a.section-credit (the verbatim imagery attribution link, :2441-2459) and div.section-structure-chip (the selected/hovered structure name — the ONLY selection feedback on this surface, :2603-2609). Internal precedent, same repo: scripts/verify/ax-delta.mjs:6-14 records that the plate root used to be role="img" and therefore "the [data-structure] regions were mouse-only and contributed ZERO interactive nodes"; it was changed to a named role="group", and scripts/verify/a11y-contract.mjs:207-208 now asserts `className="plate-root" … role="group" … aria-label`. The live-section wrapper still carries the retired pattern while holding MORE interactive nodes than the plate root did.
findings.suggestedFix: Change the wrapper to role="group" with the same aria-label (one attribute, the plate-root precedent), then confirm the four children appear in the AX tree. If the group role is judged wrong for an image-like surface, move the lobes toggle, the plate chip, the credit link and the structure chip out of the wrapper instead — the wrapper must not have presentational children either way.
findings.notes: Why the defect survived: the browser lane's AX audit (§H "every interactive node has a computed accessible name") cannot see inside an AX atom — an atom contributes no child nodes, so nothing is unnamed and nothing fails. That is the same mechanism ax-delta.mjs documents for the plate. Consequence for a screen-reader user: the cortical-division layer cannot be switched on at all from this surface (it is the only control for that layer in the app), the nearest-plate chip is unreachable, the attribution link is unreachable, and the live section never announces which structure was selected — while the keyboard tree/search path still reaches selection, so the app is not unusable, only silently lossy. Verified present in the shipped bundle too: dist/assets/index-DayLESCm.js contains the literals `section-structure-chip`, `section-lobes-toggle`, `section-plate-chip`, `section-credit` and `role:"img"` (the a11y gate's bundle spot check covers none of them).

findings.subject: The four All on / All off module buttons — WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name
findings.field: button[data-header-action="areas-all-on"|"areas-all-off"|"systems-all-on"|"systems-all-off"] (src/components/Header.tsx:246-306)
findings.claimed: README L1039-1042 states the v11/v12 header controls carry "an accessible name whose visible text is a prefix (WCAG 2.5.3)"; README L1254 records that this is violated by exactly the four All-module buttons and that the violation is pinned by verify:area-toggles.
findings.expected: The accessible name must contain the visible label text (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.3, Level AA), so a speech-input user saying the words on screen activates the control.
findings.basis: Measured this session, `npm run verify:area-toggles` group 7 prints: `[a11y·PINNED DEFECT] WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) fails for exactly 4 of 5 action button(s): "All on" ∩ "All areas on — show every area" · "All off" ∩ "All areas off — hide every area" · "All on" ∩ "All systems on — show every system" · "All off" ∩ "All systems off — hide every system"`. `"All areas on — show every area".includes("All on")` is false in both directions (the name inserts a word inside the visible label). Source: Header.tsx:251, :262, :289, :300. Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.3.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the visible text a prefix of the name without inserting a word: aria-label="All on — every area" / "All off — every area" / "All on — every system" / "All off — every system". GATE COUPLING (plan D7): this flips the pinned assertion at scripts/verify/area-toggles.mjs:1385-1399 ("the four All-module buttons are the ONLY header controls whose accessible name misses its visible text (pinned defect)") and the README L1254 row — the integrator must list the gate-flip handoff and final-review must re-pin it to the fixed strings.
findings.notes: This is the one a11y defect the repo already knows about, and the finding is filed to route it, not to re-discover it. The three sibling rows are clean: 13 of 13 area/system/region buttons have names that start with their visible text (measured in the same run: "Tracts — show/hide the tract system (tract)", "Cranial nerves — show/hide the nerve system (nerve)", "Vasculature — show/hide the vasculature system", …).

findings.subject: --text-muted (#64748b) is used as body text everywhere but measures 3.73:1
findings.field: --text-muted: #64748b (src/styles/tokens.css:20); consumers: .hint (base.css:155-158), .panel-title (:147-153), .searchbox-empty/.searchbox-more (panels.css:77-82), .searchbox-via (:67-75), .legend-note (:645-648), .modal-foot (:518-521), .section-toolbar-label (plates.css:357-362), .section-alignment-note (:407-412), .plate-chip-sub (:185-189), .ruler-y (:67-72)
findings.claimed: The token is the app's muted/secondary text colour and is applied to real sentences (hints, the toolbar's alignment and imagery-off notes, the level ruler's coordinates, each plate chip's orientation line).
findings.expected: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum, AA) requires >= 4.5:1 for normal text; these runs are 0.68-0.8 rem (10.2-12 px), i.e. normal text, not large text.
findings.basis: Computed from the token hexes with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula: #64748b vs --bg-panel #101827 = 3.73:1; vs --bg-elevated #16202f = 3.44:1; vs --bg-page #0b1220 = 3.93:1; over the viewer panel's own 88 %-opaque fill (color-mix(bg-panel 88 %, transparent) over the #1b2436 gradient, viewer.css:55) it is ~3.6:1. All three surfaces fail 4.5:1. Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise --text-muted to a value that clears 4.5:1 on --bg-elevated (the darkest surface it is painted on): #94a3b8 (--text-secondary) measures 6.39:1 there and 6.93:1 on --bg-panel, which collapses two tokens into one but is the cheapest correct fix; alternatively keep the token and stop using it for text longer than a label.
findings.notes: This is a token-level fix that repairs ~10 selectors at once. It is a genuine AA failure, not a stylistic preference: the affected strings include the CT-coverage honesty sentences and the "approximate alignment" note — the surfacing of which is a product goal. Note the second-order risk: --text-secondary #94a3b8 is already used for adjacent text (e.g. .section-alignment-note's neighbours), so merging the tokens would flatten the hierarchy; a distinct token at ~#8b9bb0 is the alternative.

findings.subject: Vessel palette falls below the 3:1 non-text floor on both surfaces it encodes
findings.field: --kind-vessel: #b91c1c (src/styles/tokens.css:39); the per-record shades named at Legend.tsx:49-53 ("#dc2626 distal, #991b1b deep/vertebral"); painted as the section-canvas contour stroke/fill (SectionCanvas.tsx:1921,1925,1933,1937) and as the legend swatch (Legend.tsx:98-103, panels.css:625-631)
findings.claimed: Legend.tsx:49-53 documents the arterial family's three crimson shades as the palette convention, and the legend swatch is the app's statement of what that colour means.
findings.expected: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 (Non-text Contrast, AA) requires >= 3:1 between a graphical object required to understand the content and its adjacent colour. The legend swatch (11x11 px, .legend-swatch) and the vessel contour stroke are exactly that.
findings.basis: Computed from the hexes: on --bg-panel #101827 — #b91c1c = 2.75:1, #991b1b = 2.14:1, #dc2626 = 3.68:1 (passes). On the section canvas' own BACKGROUND = '#0d1526' (SectionCanvas.tsx:372, painted at :1604; the wrap is also #0d1526 in plates.css:427) — #b91c1c = 2.82:1, #991b1b = 2.19:1, #dc2626 = 3.77:1. Two of the three documented shades fail on both surfaces; the failing pair is the one used for the trunks, the midline links and the vertebral artery, i.e. the vessels a reader most often needs to identify.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise the family's two dark shades to the #dc2626-class value that already passes (>= 3.4:1 on both surfaces), or add a light 1 px halo/outline stroke for vessel-kind contours on the canvas (the pattern already used for text knockouts) so the boundary, not the fill, carries the contrast.
findings.notes: Not a rendering finding (the material factory is audit-rendering's scope): this is filed as a UX/legibility one because the palette token is the app's legend contract. Related, measured and PASSING: --selection #f59e0b = 8.27:1 on --bg-panel and 8.49:1 on the canvas background, so the selection stroke is not part of this problem.

findings.subject: Every .btn's boundary collapses to 1.55:1 and its fill to 1.08:1 against the panel behind it
findings.field: .btn (src/styles/base.css:87-100): background --bg-elevated #16202f, border 1px --border-strong #2c3a52, on --bg-panel #101827 (header, sidebar, toolbar) and on the 88 %-opaque viewer panel
findings.claimed: The shared button primitive is the boundary of every control in the header (Areas/Systems/All modules/quality/References), the Plates toolbar, the tree and the PiP size controls.
findings.expected: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 requires >= 3:1 for the visual information needed to identify a UI component. With a fill that is 1.08:1 against its background, the 1 px border IS the identifying information.
findings.basis: Computed: #16202f (button fill) vs #101827 (panel) = 1.08:1; #2c3a52 (--border-strong, the button's only edge) vs #101827 = 1.55:1. Neither reaches 3:1. The pressed state is fine by contrast (`.btn.is-active` border becomes --accent #38bdf8 = 8.29:1), so the failure is specific to the unpressed/default button, i.e. to every control before the user has touched it. Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken or lighten --border-strong for interactive borders (measured candidates on --bg-panel: #4b5f80 = 2.75:1, #556a8c = 3.24:1, #5b7093 = 3.54:1 - so #556a8c is the cheapest passing value) and/or raise the button fill's separation from the panel; check the same token where it is decorative (.searchbox-input border, .plate-chip, .section-canvas-wrap frame) so the divider lines do not become loud.
findings.notes: The 3:1 applicability clause ("required to identify") is an interpretation, and it is stated as such — the ratios are measured facts. Supporting internal evidence that the edge is load-bearing: `.btn`'s fill is deliberately one step (1.08:1) from the panel, so removing the border would leave the controls invisible; and the repo's own a11y contract already treats control boundaries as contractual (it asserts >= 24 px hit targets and a focus ring, a11y-contract.mjs:334-347, but has no border-contrast assertion).

findings.subject: Dimmed taxonomy-tree rows drop enabled text to 3.31:1
findings.field: .tree-leaf-row.is-off { opacity: 0.4 } (src/styles/panels.css:189-191) and .tree-region.is-off > .tree-region-row { opacity: 0.45 } (:100-102); text colour --text-primary #e5e7eb on --bg-panel #101827
findings.claimed: Tree rows whose region/kind layer is off are dimmed to show that the layer is off (TaxonomyTree.tsx:23-25,39,50), while the row stays clickable and is the app's main keyboard browse path.
findings.expected: The row is an ENABLED control carrying information; WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 requires >= 4.5:1 for its text. (The "inactive component" exemption does not apply: selecting the row still works and still opens the record.)
findings.basis: Composited (opacity over the panel, no blend): 0.4 x #e5e7eb over #101827 = #656b75 = 3.31:1; 0.45 x #e5e7eb = #70757f = 3.84:1. Both below 4.5:1. Measured by compositing the token alpha onto the token background and re-running the WCAG formula.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise the dim to opacity 0.55 (measured 5.12:1; 0.5 measures 4.48:1 and still misses, 0.6 measures 5.84:1) and let the border-left/background state carry the rest of the distinction, or dim only the row's chrome (glyph/border) and keep the name at full contrast.
findings.notes: The all-off state is reachable in one click (the "All off" module sets every region off), so the majority of the tree can be in this state while remaining the only way to turn an individual structure's layer back on — the state where legibility matters most. Related PASSING measurement: the header's row labels (.header-row-label, opacity 0.65 on #e5e7eb) composite to 6.67:1.

findings.subject: PiP header controls are named by their glyphs (X / Y / Z / ▴ / ▾ / ×)
findings.field: button.pip-btn in src/components/viewer3d/SectionPiP.tsx:760-791 — axis buttons carry only `{axis.toUpperCase()}` (:768), the size button only `{preset === 'large' ? '▾' : '▴'}` (:782), the hide button only `×` (:790); the explanatory text sits in `title` (:776-779, :787) and in a non-focusable span's title (:759)
findings.claimed: SectionPiP.tsx:20-24 states the panel's chrome contract as "the `X` / `Y` / `Z` axis override buttons with `aria-pressed` … `×` (hide, `title=\"Hide live section\"`)", and the panel's own header comment argues the a11y lane requires every control to be named.
findings.expected: Each control needs an accessible name that states its purpose. Under the accessible-name computation, an element's CONTENT is used before its title, so these buttons are named "X", "Y", "Z", "▴", "▾", "×" and the purpose sentence never reaches assistive technology (title becomes the description, if anything).
findings.basis: AccName 1.2 / HTML-AAM name computation order: aria-label, then host-language labelling, then name-from-content, and only last the title attribute — so `title` cannot override content. Source evidence: no `aria-label` appears anywhere in SectionPiP.tsx's JSX (grep of the file: the only aria-labels are `pipResizerLabel(...)` on the four resize handles, :889). Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) with SC 2.4.6/3.3.2 for the label question.
findings.suggestedFix: Add aria-label to each: axis buttons `aria-label={`Section axis ${axis.toUpperCase()} — ${view.caption}`}`, size button `aria-label={\`Panel size ${size.width}×${size.height} px\`}`, hide button `aria-label="Hide live section"`. Keep the glyphs as the visible text.
findings.notes: The four resize handles ARE correctly named from the same file (`pipResizerLabel` includes the corner and the live size, :499-506), which is what makes the omission look like an oversight rather than a policy. The group context (`role="group" aria-label="Simulated section panel …"`, :751-753) gives a screen reader the panel, not the button's purpose. Verified absent from the a11y gate: scripts/verify/a11y-contract.mjs has no assertion on SectionPiP button names (it asserts only that the narrow-viewport toggle exists, :239-240), and the browser lane's AX pass cannot compute a name for a glyph it never sees in this sandbox.

findings.subject: The live section's hit-test has no keyboard path (pointer-only selection)
findings.field: canvas.section-canvas (src/components/section/SectionCanvas.tsx:2386-2392): onPointerMove/onPointerLeave/onClick only — no tabIndex, no onKeyDown, no role=button; the wrapper is role="img" (:2383)
findings.claimed: v16d documents the single-click contract as a primary interaction: "ONE click does both jobs" — it places the crosshair and selects the structure under the pointer (SectionCanvas.tsx:2282-2293).
findings.expected: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard): all functionality must be operable through a keyboard interface. Selection IS reachable by keyboard elsewhere (the tree and the search box both call the same `selectStructure`), so the requirement is met by an equivalent alternative; what is missing is any keyboard route to the SECTION-specific part (per-structure hit-testing on the slice, and crosshair placement at a point).
findings.basis: Judgment, informed by WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1's "except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement" carve-out and by the availability of the tree/search alternative. The section's own plane control DOES have a keyboard path (SectionSliderBar's three named range inputs, SectionSliderBar.tsx:118-132), so only the point-and-click selection is pointer-bound.
findings.suggestedFix: Lowest-cost honest option: state the limitation where the feature is described (a title/aria-description on the canvas wrapper naming the keyboard alternative), or add a structure list beside the live section ordered by the canvas' draw order so keyboard users can walk the same structures. A full keyboard hit-test is not worth building.
findings.notes: Filed as suspect rather than wrong precisely because the alternative exists — this is not a conformance failure on its own. It becomes a real gap in combination with ux-001 (the wrapper's role="img" means a screen-reader user is not even told that the surface is interactive) and with ux-025 (no on-screen text says the surface is clickable at all).

findings.subject: The tab bar declares role="tablist"/role="tab" but does not implement the tabs pattern, and holds a non-tab child
findings.field: div.center-tabs[role="tablist"] (src/App.tsx:178-206): three button[role="tab"] with aria-selected + aria-controls="center-body" and no roving tabindex / no keydown handler; plus button.center-tabs-browse (a plain toggle button, :197-205) inside the tablist; div#center-body[role="tabpanel"][aria-label="Active view"] (:208) is not referenced by aria-labelledby
findings.claimed: The three views are presented as tabs (labels "3D", "Plates", "Syndromes", titles at App.tsx:84-88); the Browse button is a fifth control docked in the same bar.
findings.expected: The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices tabs pattern requires: only the selected tab in the tab order (roving tabindex), Left/Right arrow keys to move between tabs, Home/End optionally, and only role="tab" elements owned by the tablist. The panel should be associated with its tab (aria-labelledby).
findings.basis: Standard: WAI-ARIA 1.2 / APG Tabs pattern (keyboard interaction and required owned elements). Source: every tab is focusable (no tabIndex prop anywhere in App.tsx), no onKeyDown exists in the file, and .center-tabs-browse is a child of the element carrying role="tablist".
findings.suggestedFix: Either implement the pattern (tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1} + arrow-key handler + aria-labelledby on the panel) or drop the ARIA (a plain group of buttons with aria-pressed, which is what the markup actually behaves like). Move the Browse toggle out of the tablist element in both cases.
findings.notes: Operability itself is fine — Tab + Enter reaches every view, so this is not a 2.1.1 failure; it is a pattern-conformance defect that makes the widget announce differently from how it behaves (a screen reader says "tab 1 of 3, use arrow keys", and arrow keys do nothing).

findings.subject: The level ruler marks the current level visually only — no aria-current
findings.field: button.ruler-item.is-current (src/components/LevelRuler.tsx:54-70; style src/styles/plates.css:40-43); the label is `shortLevelName(level.name)` + `y` (:68-69), the plate/y detail is title-only (:61-65)
findings.claimed: LevelRuler.tsx:5-6: "The level nearest the current clip.y stays highlighted, so moving the 3D plane keeps the ruler in sync."
findings.expected: The current item of a set should be exposed programmatically (aria-current="true" on the current level, or aria-pressed if the control is read as a toggle) so the sync is perceivable without seeing the accent border.
findings.basis: Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) / 4.1.2 — the state exists in the store (`nearestLevel`, LevelRuler.tsx:31-42) and in the DOM only as a CSS class. Contrast of the marker itself PASSES (.ruler-item.is-current: accent border 8.29:1 + a tinted background, plates.css:40-43), so this is a state-exposure defect, not a visibility one.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `aria-current={isCurrent ? 'true' : undefined}` to the ruler button; it costs one attribute and makes "which level am I on" answerable from the keyboard and from a screen reader.
findings.notes: The accessible name of each ruler item is already reasonable ("Mesencephalon +6" style: short label + signed y), and the title carries the full level name and the plate id, so a screen-reader user can navigate the list — they just cannot tell where the 3D plane is. The same asymmetry exists for the Legend's kind/region toggles, but there it is carried by a real checkbox's checked state, so only the ruler is affected.

findings.subject: The taxonomy tree's selection and syndrome states are conveyed by colour alone and by no ARIA state
findings.field: .tree-leaf-row.is-selected { background: rgba(245,158,11,0.14); border-left-color: var(--selection) } and .is-in-syndrome { background: rgba(56,189,248,0.08); border-left-color: var(--accent) } (src/styles/panels.css:169-178); applied at src/components/TaxonomyTree.tsx:45-51
findings.claimed: The tree is the app's structure browser: "Rows sync with the global store: click selects …, rows whose kind/region layer is toggled off are dimmed, the selected row is marked" (TaxonomyTree.tsx:2-7).
findings.expected: The selected row must be programmatically determinable (aria-current="true", or aria-selected inside a listbox/tree role) and, per SC 1.4.1, selection should not be conveyed by colour alone.
findings.basis: Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 + 4.1.2 (state not exposed) and SC 1.4.1 (colour as the only visual means: the row's text, glyph and weight are identical between selected and unselected rows; only the tint and border-left colour change). Source: the row is a plain button with no aria-pressed/aria-current/aria-selected (TaxonomyTree.tsx:43-61). Internal contradiction: the same component DOES expose expansion state correctly (aria-expanded on .tree-region-row and .tree-sub-row, :120, :137) — so the omission is inconsistent within one file.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `aria-current={selected ? 'true' : undefined}` to tree-leaf-row; optionally add a non-colour cue (a ▸ marker or a bold name) to satisfy 1.4.1 for the syndrome state as well.
findings.notes: Selection IS announced elsewhere: the info panel's heading changes to the record name and (on desktop) the panel is visible, so a screen-reader user is not left without the information — they simply cannot find it IN the tree, which is the one surface where "which row am I on" is the navigation question. The syndrome tint is additionally redundant with the syndrome card's own text and the 3D dimming.

findings.subject: aria-label on role-less divs: the plate strip and the imaging-sources group are not actually labelled
findings.field: div.plate-strip[aria-label="Plate picker"] (src/components/PlatesTab.tsx:504) and div.section-toolbar-group.section-link-chips[aria-label="Imaging sources"] (:712)
findings.claimed: The two rows present themselves as labelled groups (the phrasing is the same as the neighbouring real groups, which do carry role="group": "Orientation filter" :453, "Section axis" :558, "Imagery modality" :583, "CT window preset" :641, "MRI intensity window" :675).
findings.expected: aria-label is only honoured on elements whose role supports naming. A `div` maps to role=generic, which does not, so the attribute is ignored by assistive technology and by the accessibility tree.
findings.basis: Standard: W3C ARIA in HTML (aria-label is not permitted on role=generic) and HTML-AAM's naming prohibition for the generic role. Internal evidence that the intent was a labelled group: five sibling containers in the same two files do carry role="group".
findings.suggestedFix: Add role="group" to both divs (one attribute each), matching their siblings.
findings.notes: No functional loss for pointer or keyboard users (the chips are ordinary buttons/links and the strip is horizontally scrollable with .plate-chip min-width 118 px, plates.css:157-168). This is filed because the plate strip is one of the surfaces the brief names ("the plate chips") and because an unlabelled strip is indistinguishable from an unlabelled pile of buttons when a screen reader lists the tab stops.

findings.subject: The CT window <select> has no programmatic label; its name comes from title and does not contain the visible label text
findings.field: select.section-select (src/components/PlatesTab.tsx:644-664): no id/label/aria-label; the visible label is the sibling span.section-toolbar-label "CT window" (:642) inside div[role="group"][aria-label="CT window preset"] (:641)
findings.claimed: The group name and the title explain the control (title text at :648-652).
findings.expected: A form control must have a programmatically associated label; its accessible name should contain the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3). Here the name falls back to the title ("Display window for the CT modality (Hounsfield units, from ct-manifest.json) — ignored while MRI or a photograph is drawn"), which does not contain "CT window".
findings.basis: Standard: HTML-AAM name computation for select (no label element and no aria-label → title is the last-resort name) + WCAG 2.1 SC 3.3.2 (Labels or Instructions) and SC 2.5.3; the visible text "CT window" is one association away from being the name. Source: the sibling `<span>` is text-only and not associated.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the select `aria-label="CT window"` (the visible string) and keep the title as the description.
findings.notes: The same pattern is CORRECT in SectionSliderBar, where each range input carries `aria-label={`${slider.label} plane position (atlas units)`}` starting with the visible text (SectionSliderBar.tsx:128) — so the fix is to copy an existing in-repo idiom. Also note the select renders disabled when CT is not installed (:647), which is the correct state and is announced.

findings.subject: Wrapping <label> around a range and an <output> leaks the live value into the control's accessible name
findings.field: label.section-opacity-slider (src/components/PlatesTab.tsx:625-637: "Opacity" + input[type=range] + output), and the MRI window pair (:677-692 "Low", :693-708 "High"); the same structure in the CT/MRI readouts
findings.claimed: The label names the control ("Opacity", "Low", "High") and the output shows its value.
findings.expected: A control's accessible name should be stable and should not contain its own value (the value is announced separately by the role). Under name-from-content, both the label text and the output's text are concatenated.
findings.basis: Standard: AccName 1.2 name-from-content walks all descendant text, and <output> contributes its text content; the resulting name is e.g. "Opacity 65 %", which changes on every drag. Source: the <output> sits INSIDE the <label> element in all three controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the <output> outside the <label> (wrapping div + htmlFor on the label), or add an explicit aria-label="Opacity" to the range input so the computed name stops moving.
findings.notes: The ExplodeSlider already does this correctly — `<label htmlFor="explode-range">Explode</label>` is a sibling, not a wrapper, and the range carries aria-label="Exploded view factor" (ExplodeSlider.tsx:15-25) — so two idioms for the same widget exist in the same app. Note the more serious version of this class is the PiP toggle's visually-hidden checkbox (SectionPiP.tsx:805-818), where the label text + readout ARE the name by design and the panel's own comment defends it (:793-804); that one is intentional and is NOT filed.

findings.subject: The search listbox's children are not all options
findings.field: ul#searchbox-results[role="listbox"] (src/components/SearchBox.tsx:99-132) contains li.searchbox-empty (:100-102), li[role="option"] (:103-128) and li.searchbox-more (:129-131)

findings.expected: A listbox's owned children must be option (or group) elements; non-option children are dropped from the accessibility tree (or announced as an empty listbox), which matters most for the actionable strings "No structure matches … — try a synonym" and "Showing 12 of 40 — keep typing to narrow".

findings.suggestedFix: Give the two informational rows role="presentation" and move their text into a sibling live region (or into the input's aria-describedby), or render them outside the listbox element.
findings.notes: Everything else about this combobox measures correct and is asserted by `scripts/verify/a11y-contract.mjs` (aria-activedescendant + stable `searchbox-option-<id>` ids, 2 assertions passed in this session's run). Keyboard support (ArrowUp/Down/Enter/Escape) is implemented at SearchBox.tsx:56-71; Home/End are not, which the APG lists as optional.

findings.subject: The search input's :focus rule cancels the app-wide :focus-visible ring
findings.field: .searchbox-input:focus { border-color: var(--accent); outline: none } (src/styles/panels.css:25-28) vs the global :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px } (src/styles/base.css:74-78)
findings.claimed: Every control has a visible focus indicator (base.css supplies one globally; a11y-contract.mjs asserts bespoke rings for the plate regions and labels, :335-338).
findings.expected: The focused search field must show a visible indicator (WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7). Removing the outline leaves only a 1 px border-colour change, which is a weaker and less conventional indicator than the ring every other control gets.
findings.basis: Specificity arithmetic on the shipped stylesheets: `.searchbox-input:focus` = (0,1,1) beats `:focus-visible` = (0,1,0), so `outline: none` wins for this element in both focus states; the file therefore has NO outline in any state. The adjacent border does change to --accent #38bdf8 (8.29:1 on the panel), so the indicator is not invisible — it is inconsistent with the rest of the app and 1 px wide. Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7.
findings.suggestedFix: Scope the reset to pointer focus only (`:focus:not(:focus-visible)`) or delete `outline: none` and let the global ring paint; keep the border-colour change as an additional cue.
findings.notes: The a11y gate's CSS contract reads the plate and PiP focus rules and the global ring exists in base.css, so nothing in the current gate set can catch a per-selector `outline: none` override — this is a concrete example of the "check that passes by not running" pattern the run's ground rules name.

findings.subject: The "● live" active-axis marker is CSS-generated content inside a <label>; whether it reaches the accessible name is not verifiable here
findings.field: .slider-row.is-active-axis label::after { content: '● live' … } (src/styles/viewer.css:94-104), applied to the ClipControls and SectionSliderBar labels; the file's own comment says "Decorative 'live' marker; the label text itself is unchanged for assistive tech."
findings.claimed: viewer.css:91-93 — the marker is decorative and does not change the label text for assistive technology.
findings.expected: If browsers include ::after content in the name-from-content walk (Chrome, Firefox and Safari all do in current versions), the accessible name of the sagittal range input becomes "Sagittal · x ● live" while the inactive rows read "Sagittal · x" — i.e. the comment is wrong and the state is exposed twice (in the name and visually). If they do not, the comment is right and the live state is visual-only (a 1.3.1 concern).
findings.basis: No browser and no accessibility-tree dump is available in this sandbox (Chrome cannot start here, and this session has no browser lane). The claim depends on runtime name computation, which I cannot execute; the AccName specification does not settle pseudo-element content explicitly, and the two possible outcomes lead to different findings. No fix is proposed because the correct fix depends on which outcome holds.
findings.suggestedFix: None until measured. When a browser lane is available: read the computed name of #clip-sagittal and #section-slider-sagittal with the axis active, and either (a) replace the ::after with an aria-hidden span if the name changed, or (b) add an explicit aria-description/aria-label if the state is missing.
findings.notes: Recorded rather than dropped so the question is not silently lost; the same mechanism applies to any other CSS-generated state marker in the app (grep found this as the only `::after` that adds words to a labelled control).

findings.subject: The 12 cranial-nerve records' authored `course` and `modality` text is unreachable in the product
findings.field: StructureRecord.course (src/types.ts:85) and .modality (:84); data: src/data/structures/brainstem-cranial-nerves.json (10 records) + telencephalon-cranial-nerves.json (2); consumer: none
findings.claimed: types.ts:70-83 states the two fields are "the two facts a reader needs and neither `function` nor `connections` can carry without turning into prose"; README L39 sells exactly them as the v13 payoff ("each record carries its modality, its course *with the skull-base foramen it uses*"). SceneLayers.tsx:711-713 asserts that "`origin3d`, `size3d`, `function`, `modality`, `course` and the clinical items are still read by the InfoPanel".
findings.expected: A delivered, validated content field must be rendered by some surface, or its being delivered must not be claimed. Measured: every one of the 12 records authors a substantial `course` (876-1290 characters each, e.g. nrv-cn7-facial names the internal acoustic meatus, the geniculate ganglion, the external genu, the nerve to stapedius, the chorda tympani and the stylomastoid foramen) and a `modality`; InfoPanel renders neither.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction, established by exhaustive search: grep for `\.course` / `modality` across src/components returns no reader of `record.course` or `record.modality` for StructureRecord (the only `modality` rendering is TractDetails, InfoPanel.tsx:287-288, which is the TractRecord branch; the `course` hits in sectionAssets.ts/SceneLayers.ts are loop variables over course TABLES, not the record field). InfoPanel's StructureDetails renders function, territory, connections, clinical, bloodSupply, levels, syndromes, contextNote, refs (:207-266) — the list has no course and no modality. The catalogue-shaped consequence: the app can tell a user the foramen a nerve uses only if that fact happens to be in `function`.
findings.suggestedFix: Add two InfoPanel sections for structure records ("Course" and "Modality") in the same style as the existing "Blood supply"/"Context note" blocks, gated on the field being present — a rendering-only change, no data edit.
findings.notes: This is the largest single UX loss found: a whole authored dimension of the v13/v14 content set is invisible. It is filed here (not as a facts/features finding) because the deliverable is a reading surface. Overlaps with audit-features' content-inventory scope by design; the evidence here is the absence of any consumer, which is a UI fact. Note also that the course narrative is long-form prose, so the fix must not break the panel's density (a collapsed <details> or a max-height block is the cheap answer).

findings.subject: 9 of 12 nerve "Context note" texts describe the schematic ellipsoid that v14 stopped drawing
findings.field: record.contextNote rendered by InfoPanel.tsx:256-261 as "Context note"; the nine records whose note contains "a sized schematic ellipsoid" / "The ellipsoid at origin3d …": nrv-cn4-trochlear, cn5-trigeminal, cn6-abducens, cn7-facial, cn8-vestibulocochlear, cn9-glossopharyngeal, cn10-vagus, cn11-accessory, cn12-hypoglossal
findings.claimed: The note is the record's own honesty statement about what the reader is looking at — e.g. nrv-cn6-abducens: "this record is `meshes: false` with a sized schematic ellipsoid and no manifest or section part. The ellipsoid at origin3d [4.5, -18, 5] with radii size3d [1.6, 9, 2] spans y ~ -27…-9 au, a long thin vertical body that stands for the nerve's ascending cisternal course".
findings.expected: The note must describe the object actually drawn. Since v14 the drawn object is the authored course tube, and SceneLayers.tsx:736 returns null (no ellipsoid) for any record where `hasNerveCourse(record.id)` is true — which is all 12 (verified: each of the 12 ids appears in src/geometry/curves.ts' NERVE_COURSES table).
findings.basis: Internal contradiction: SceneLayers.tsx:695-713 states the ellipsoid is suppressed for every course-bearing nerve ("a nerve that now has a COURSE must not also keep its schematic placement ellipsoid: one record, one body") and README L1329-1331 states the shipped XOR table prints `marker would-draw = no` for all twelve — while the in-app note for nine of them tells the reader that the ellipsoid is what they see, and for cn6 even describes its y-extent. The user-visible text is therefore wrong about the picture above it. The three records that do not carry the phrase (cn1-olfactory, cn2-optic, cn3-oculomotor) are the ones whose notes were re-authored with the course.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-point the nine notes at the drawn tube ("the drawn body is the authored course, a tapered tube from … to …; the schematic ellipsoid was retired in v14") or drop the geometry paragraph and leave the clinical caveats — either way this is a data-text edit, which the integrator owns, not a layout change.
findings.notes: The nerve records' `course` text (ux-022) already contains the correct anatomy; the cheapest coherent fix is to render `course` and trim the note's stale geometry sentence. Filed here rather than under facts because it is the panel's user-facing copy.

findings.subject: The v14 course honesty statement ("an authored path, not a segmented scan") has no in-app surface
findings.field: `anchorNote` on every NerveCourseRecord (src/geometry/curves.ts:109 declaration, :155-840 the twelve strings) and on every vessel course (src/geometry/vasculature-courses.ts:135, plus the 39 JSON rows); consumer: none

The nearest in-app honesty text is the nerve record's `contextNote` (ux-023), which speaks about the retired marker and says nothing about the course being a hand-authored path — so a user who selects CN VII is told the tube's anatomy as fact with no note that no scan was segmented.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the course record's `anchorNote` (or a one-sentence digest of it) on the surface where the course is visible: the section canvas' selected-structure chip is inside the role="img" wrapper (ux-001), so the safe place is the info panel's Course section proposed in ux-022.

The available affordance is the crosshair cursor alone, which signals "place a point", not "select a structure".

The string should live next to the other section notes so the four surfaces cannot drift.

findings.subject: The two All modules have no visible axis word; their identity depends entirely on row position
findings.field: div.header-all-module[data-row="all-areas"|"all-systems"] (src/components/Header.tsx:231-306): both contain buttons whose visible text is exactly "All on" / "All off"; the axis exists only in aria-label/title and in the wrapper's aria-label (:234, :272)

Any rename must keep those contracts or be listed as a gate-flip handoff (plan D7).

findings.subject: The two All-off buttons never show a pressed state, though their aria-pressed can be true
findings.field: button[data-header-action="areas-all-off"] className="btn" (src/components/Header.tsx:257-267) and [data-header-action="systems-all-off"] className="btn" (:295-305) with aria-pressed={allAreasOff|allSystemsOff}; the two All-on siblings DO apply `is-active` (:249, :287)
findings.claimed: The module is the v12 replacement for the retired Reset/All pair, and each button's aria-pressed reading is derived from the store (Header.tsx:191-198).
findings.expected: Visible state and programmatic state must agree: if `aria-pressed` is read as pressed, the control must look pressed. `.btn.is-active` (base.css:106-110: accent border + 20 % accent fill) is the app's one pressed-state idiom and is applied to the on-buttons.
findings.basis: Internal asymmetry inside one component: the class expression is conditional on the on-buttons and a bare string on the off-buttons. WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 is satisfied (the state IS exposed); the defect is the 1.3.1/consistency one — the same visual outcome is described by the DOM and not shown. Consequence: clicking "All off" produces no confirmation on the control itself, and it is the action whose result is an empty 3D view.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `className={`btn${allAreasOff ? ' is-active' : ''}`}` and the same for the systems module (two characters of change), or drop `is-active` from the on-buttons too and rely on the evidence in the scene — but not on one of the two.
findings.notes: A second-order reason to fix rather than drop: the pressed reading is what tells the user the app is in the documented all-off state rather than in a broken/empty one, and the all-off state is a documented edge case of the robustness audit ("All-off empty state").

findings.subject: Layer-toggle feedback is immediate and consistent across the three surfaces that carry it

findings.expected: A toggle must show its new state immediately and identically wherever it appears.
findings.basis: Source: all three idioms read the same store sets (`layers.regions` / `layers.kinds`) and paint a state change (.btn.is-active border+fill = accent #38bdf8 at 8.29:1; native checkbox checked; .pip-btn accent border/colour). The store's `toggleKindLayer`/`toggleRegionLayer`/`toggleDivision` are the only writers. Gate evidence: `verify:area-toggles` group 7 prints every control's text and its distinct accessible name; its wiring group drives the real onClick handlers.

findings.subject: Clicking a structure produces label + border + info panel in one store write
findings.field: selectStructure → .label3d.is-selected (NucleusMesh.tsx:235-241, TractTube.tsx:504-506, viewer.css:247-251), the live-section amber stroke + .section-structure-chip (SectionCanvas.tsx:2603-2609, plates.css:491-518), the tree row highlight (panels.css:169-172) and InfoPanel's heading (InfoPanel.tsx:417-426)
findings.claimed: The brief's feedback question: "does clicking a structure give immediate, unambiguous feedback (label + border + info panel)?"
findings.expected: Verified against the render paths.
findings.basis: Source: one store action per click path (3D pointer → NucleusMesh/TractTube onClick; section click → SectionCanvas.handleClick with `{ tab: null }` so the tab does not jump, :2292; tree row, search hit, plate region and syndrome chip all call the same `selectStructure`). findings.subject: Below 1024 px the header's first grid column stays 320 px while the sidebar becomes 264 px — the toggle rows sit 56 px right of the 3D view's left border
findings.field: --sidebar-w: 320px (src/styles/layout.css:35) consumed by `.app-shell` (:36) and by `.app-header { grid-template-columns: var(--sidebar-w, 320px) minmax(0,1fr) auto }` (:66-75); the ≤1024 media block sets `.app-shell { grid-template-columns: 264px minmax(0,1fr) }` (:310-318) with the literal 264 px and never redefines --sidebar-w
findings.claimed: layout.css:30-34 (v12f) — "the header aligns to it: the header spans all three columns … and the toggle rows inside it are padded by exactly this much so they start on the 3D view's left border instead of floating in the middle of the header. One declaration, so the two cannot drift." layout.css:54-65 (v12g) repeats the intent: "the header is a GRID whose first column is the sidebar's width, so the toggle rows start exactly on the sidebar's right border (the 3D view's left border) no matter how wide the brand's text is."
findings.expected: One declaration means the two values cannot drift. Measured: there are two declarations — `var(--sidebar-w)` for the header and the literal `264px` for the sidebar at ≤1024 px — so they drift by exactly 56 px at every viewport from 641 to 1024 px.
findings.basis: Static CSS arithmetic, no browser needed: a single grep for `sidebar-w` across src/styles/*.css, index.html and src/main.tsx returns exactly three hits — the token definition (layout.css:35) and its two uses (:36, :69); the ≤1024 block writes 264px as a literal (:312). The v12g comment's own words ("the two cannot drift") are contradicted by the file it sits in. This is the v12g narrow-breakpoint gap the run's brief asks to confirm open or closed: it is OPEN, and the fix is one line.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add `--sidebar-w: 264px` inside the `@media (max-width: 1024px)` block on `.app-shell`, or change that block's `grid-template-columns: 264px …` to `var(--sidebar-w)`. The first re-aligns the header at tablet widths; both keep a single source of truth.
findings.notes: Consequence at tablet widths: the Areas/Systems rows and the two All modules start 56 px to the right of the left edge of the 3D view they control, i.e. the visual argument for the alignment ("the rows start where the view starts") is defeated exactly where space is tightest. The header's own grid is otherwise correct (the 16 px padding moved onto .brand so the first column starts at x = 0, :77-82).

findings.subject: At ≤640 px the header still reserves a 320 px first column, so the shell cannot reflow to 320 px without horizontal scrolling
findings.field: .app-header grid-template-columns from layout.css:69 (unchanged by any media query) vs the ≤640 block (:356-372) which overrides only `padding: 8px 10px` and `gap`; the shell itself becomes one column (:357-363)
findings.claimed: layout.css:1-6 — "phone ≤640px with the tabs docked as a fixed bottom bar and both panels as bottom sheets"; App.tsx:21-25 repeats the responsive contract.
findings.expected: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow, AA) requires content to be presentable without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px width. At 320 px the header's content box is 320 - 20 = 300 px, but its first grid column alone demands 320 px before the 1fr row track and the `auto` actions track (References + quality toggle, min-content ≈ 190-230 px) are laid out.
findings.basis: Static arithmetic on the shipped CSS: the first column is a fixed 320 px at every width (var(--sidebar-w, 320px)), the ≤640 rule changes only padding/gap, and no rule anywhere sets a smaller value or `minmax(0, …)`. The overflow is therefore guaranteed to be at least 20 px plus whatever the rows and the actions need — i.e. it does not depend on text metrics. Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.10. (No horizontal-overflow style exists on .app-header, .app-shell or body, so the page scrolls rather than clipping.)
findings.suggestedFix: Inside the ≤640 block, reset the header to a single column (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)` with `.brand`, `.header-rows` and `.header-actions` stacked, or `grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0,1fr)` with the brand wrapping), matching the one-column shell the same block already declares.
findings.notes: This is the same declaration as ux-031 seen at the other breakpoint — one fix (making the sidebar width a per-breakpoint token AND letting the header collapse below 640) closes both. Because the visual consequence (a horizontally scrolling header) needs a browser to photograph, the finding rests on the CSS arithmetic above; the arithmetic alone is decisive here because a fixed 320 px column cannot fit a 300 px content box.

findings.subject: The header's documented line/row alignment mechanism does not exist in the code
findings.field: div.header-rows style (src/components/Header.tsx:215-218) = { display:flex, flexDirection:row, flexWrap:wrap, gap:4, minWidth:0, flex:1 } — no flexBasis on any child and no marginLeft:auto on either module; children: .header-all-module[data-row=all-areas] (order 1, :236-244), .header-all-module[data-row=all-systems] (order 3, :274-282), .header-areas (order 0, :319), .header-systems (order 2, :355)
findings.claimed: Header.tsx:207-214 (v12b) — "the Areas row is given `flexBasis: 100%` so it still owns the first line, and the Systems row plus the All on/All off module share the second line, with the module pushed to the right (`marginLeft: 'auto'`)"; Header.tsx:219-230 (v12e) — "the Areas module shares the Areas row's line (order 1, right-aligned by `marginLeft: 'auto'`) and the Systems module shares the Systems row's line (order 3, same right alignment). The Systems row itself carries `flexBasis: 100%` (order 2), which is what forces it onto a fresh line so the two groups cannot interleave."
findings.expected: If the visual grouping is load-bearing (and the comments say it is the ONLY thing that says which axis each module acts on), it must be expressed in the layout. Measured: `flexBasis` appears nowhere in Header.tsx (grep over src finds exactly one occurrence, PlatesTab.tsx:741) and `marginLeft` appears nowhere either; there is no `.header-systems` / `.header-areas` / `.header-all-module` rule in any CSS file (grep over src/styles returns nothing).
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between three comment blocks and the shipped code, established by exhaustive grep. What the code actually does: four wrapping flex items ordered 0,1,2,3, whose wrap points are emergent from content width — so at some widths the systems module can wrap away from its row and sit on a line belonging to the other group, which is precisely the failure the comments promise cannot happen ("the two groups cannot interleave", "the two cannot drift"). The 4 px gap and the 3 px/6 px padding are the only spacing facts that survive.
findings.suggestedFix: Either implement what the comments say (`flexBasis: '100%'` on the .header-systems element and `marginLeft: 'auto'` on both modules — three inline properties) or rewrite the comments to describe the emergent behaviour and drop the claim that a module's position identifies its axis. Do not leave both.
findings.notes: Cannot be settled to the pixel without a browser, and the finding does not depend on that: it is a claim/code contradiction, which is decisive on its own. Severity is major rather than minor because the missing property is the stated mechanism for a WCAG-relevant disambiguation (see ux-027) and because three independent comment blocks assert it.

findings.subject: One layer axis, two naming systems: the header says "Vessels"/"Cranial nerves", the Legend says "vessel"/"nerve"
findings.field: Header KIND_LABELS (src/components/Header.tsx:104-116): Nuclei · Tracts · Ventricles · Surface · Context · Vessels · Cranial nerves; Legend's second toggle block renders the raw ALL_KINDS entries as visible text (src/components/Legend.tsx:164-169: `{kind}` → "nucleus · tract · ventricle · surface · vessel · context · nerve") and the raw regions (:170-175 → "telencephalon · diencephalon · midbrain · pons · medulla · cerebellum · vasculature")
findings.claimed: Both blocks are the SAME axis: ALL_KINDS/ALL_REGIONS mapped, as the Legend's own header states ("quick layer toggles that mirror the store's region/kind layer sets", Legend.tsx:2-4) and as load.ts:222-229 documents ("`Header.tsx` maps `ALL_KINDS` into the `data-kind` buttons … and `Legend.tsx` maps it into the per-kind checkboxes, so a kind added here appears in both rows with no other UI edit").
findings.expected: One axis should have one name per object. Two of the seven kinds are named materially differently across the two controls — "Vessels" vs "vessel" and, worse, "Cranial nerves" vs "nerve" — and the Legend exposes the internal slugs (also seen in the info panel's kind chip, InfoPanel.tsx:40-44, and in the header's aria-labels, e.g. "show/hide the nerve system (nerve)").
findings.basis: Internal: the two renderers read the same constant and produce different strings for the same object (exact strings quoted above; measured in `verify:area-toggles` group 7, which prints the header's seven visible labels). Judgment is involved only in the severity: a reader can still infer the mapping, and the tree/plate/search surfaces use display names throughout.
findings.suggestedFix: Give Legend its own display-label lookup (KIND_LABELS-shape, shared with Header rather than duplicated — the header's `KIND_LABELS` is already an exhaustive `Record<Kind, string>`, so exporting it from the store and importing it in both places removes the second vocabulary) and use REGION_LABELS for the region rows. Keep the slug in the aria-label only where a gate needs it.
findings.notes: The region rows have the same shape of problem but a milder one: REGION_LABELS already exists with display names ("Telencephalon (cerebral hemispheres)", "Mesencephalon (midbrain)", load.ts:232-240) and the Legend ignores it. Careful with the header contract before renaming: README L1154 documents that exactly two header controls read "Nuclei" and two read "All", and the browser lane addresses some controls by exact text — any rename is a gate-flip handoff (plan D7).

findings.subject: Product name says "Brainstem Atlas" and the subtitle says "midbrain" while every control says "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" and the scope includes the telencephalon
findings.field: h1.app-title "NeuroAxis" + span.app-subtitle "3D Brainstem Atlas — diencephalon · midbrain · rhombencephalon · telencephalon" (src/components/Header.tsx:203-204); index.html:18 `<title>NeuroAxis — 3D Brainstem Atlas: Diencephalon · Mesencephalon · Rhombencephalon</title>`; package.json:6 description; vs REGION_LABELS.midbrain = "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" (load.ts:235), AREAS label "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" (store.ts:1226), DIVISIONS label "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" (store.ts:1061)
findings.claimed: The atlas is presented as a brainstem atlas with a telencephalon extension.
findings.expected: Terminology should be stable across surfaces, and the name should not contradict the content: the largest single region in the registry is the telencephalon (85 of 236 rows at v11, per README L1046) and the v7/v8/v13 waves added hemispheres, basal ganglia, limbic structures, white matter, vasculature and cranial nerves.
findings.basis: Internal: three labels for the same object - "midbrain" in the header subtitle (Header.tsx:204), "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" in the region/area/division tables (load.ts:235, store.ts:1061, store.ts:1226) and "Mesencephalon" in the page title (index.html:18); the index.html meta description (:8) follows the page title's form. Plus a product name that understates the shipped scope. Judgment on the naming call; the inconsistency itself is a fact.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one: use "Mesencephalon (midbrain)" wherever there is room and "Midbrain" where there is not — never both in one string (index.html:18 says "Mesencephalon", Header.tsx:204 says "midbrain"). For the title, either rename to the whole-brain scope or state the extension explicitly ("… with telencephalon and vasculature").
findings.notes: Note that README's own heading uses the full name ("NeuroAxis — 3D Brainstem Atlas: Diencephalon · Mesencephalon · Rhombencephalon"), so the drift is inside index.html versus Header.tsx versus the data tables rather than docs versus code.

findings.subject: "au" (atlas units) is displayed in five surfaces and defined in none
findings.field: LevelRuler title `y = ${level.y} au` (LevelRuler.tsx:63) with span.ruler-y printing the bare number (:69); ClipControls' three <output>s ("+12", ":100-142"); SectionSliderBar's readouts ("+12.0 au", SectionSliderBar.tsx:53-56); the PiP readout ("y = 12.0 au", SectionPiP.tsx:757) and its size title ("224x170 px", :777); the plate chip ("≈ Pons middle (2.4 au) — open", SectionCanvas.tsx:2600); plate-chip sub-lines ("transverse · y = 12", PlatesTab.tsx:517-520)
findings.claimed: The unit is part of the app's readouts (the audits even pin the string shape: "x = 12.0 au").
findings.expected: A unit that appears in six places should be expandable somewhere in the UI — the only textual definition in the repo is in code comments and manifest JSON ("1 au = 1.2 mm", e.g. src/geometry/curves.ts:10, clipPlanes.ts), plus "atlas units" inside one aria-label (SectionSliderBar.tsx:128).
findings.basis: Judgment, supported by an exhaustive search: the strings "1 au = 1.2 mm" and "atlas unit" occur only in .ts/.json comments and in the single aria-label above — never in visible copy. Whether a domain-appropriate reader needs the expansion is a legibility judgment; the fact that the number is uninterpretable on screen (is +12 mm? cm? a level?) is not.
findings.suggestedFix: One definition line where the ruler and readouts live, e.g. in the level ruler's existing hint (LevelRuler.tsx:50) or as the ClipControls panel's first hint: "1 au = 1.2 mm; y is the rostro-caudal axis". Cheap, and it makes the level ruler's numbers actionable for a reader who does not already know the atlas' frame.
findings.notes: Not filed as wrong because the abbreviation is used consistently and a neuroanatomy reader may well infer "atlas unit" from context; filed as suspect because the audit's own ground rules require a basis, and the only basis here is legibility judgment — labelled as such.

findings.subject: "Clinical motor" inside the Systems row is a view framing, not a system — documented, and labelled as such
findings.field: button[data-header-action="clinical-motor"] in .header-systems (src/components/Header.tsx:407-417), aria-label "Clinical motor — brainstem motor nuclei and the descending motor pathways", title = VIEW_PRESETS['clinical-motor'].hint, toggling to 'all' when already active
findings.claimed: Header.tsx:400-406 — "the one framing that is not a single area or kind, kept as a category in this row (the user asked for exactly this one to survive the preset row's removal)"; v12's brief asked for Clinical motor as a Systems category.
findings.expected: A category that is not a kind should be distinguishable from the kinds it sits beside, and must not silently do something different (it is a preset: it rewrites regions AND kinds AND hidden).
findings.basis: Source: the button is the only one in the row backed by `VIEW_PRESETS` and it says so in its accessible name ("… brainstem motor nuclei and the descending motor pathways") and in its title (the preset's own hint); its toggle-off branch returns to the documented all-on framing rather than to an undefined state (:414). Its `data-header-action` hook distinguishes it for the browser lane. Measured present in `verify:area-toggles` group 7's control list ("Clinical motor" among the 5 action buttons).
findings.suggestedFix: None required. Optional polish: a small visible cue that it is a preset (e.g. the `.header-row-label` idiom, or moving it after a 1 px separator) so it is not read as an eighth system.
findings.notes: Filed as ok explicitly because the brief asks about "Vasculature vs Vessels vs Cranial nerves in the Systems row" — the three names there are correct for three different objects (a region-backed system: "Vasculature"; a kind: "Vessels"; another kind: "Cranial nerves"), and the store DERIVES the region-backed button as the complement of AREAS (store.ts:1236-1238), so no region is claimed twice. The related documentation drift (README L1152 still says "The six areas") is a README claim, not a UI one, and is left to the code-quality auditor's doc sweep.

findings.subject: The info panel landmark has no accessible name, and its visible heading disappears on phones
findings.field: aside.info-panel (src/components/InfoPanel.tsx:390-398) with h2.panel-title "Selection details" (:400); layout.css:468-470 hides `.info-panel-bar .panel-title` at ≤640 px, leaving only button.sheet-toggle (:472-475)
findings.claimed: The right rail is the record reader; on phones it becomes a bottom sheet with a drag-bar header carrying the selected record's name (InfoPanel.tsx:401-409).
findings.expected: A landmark region should be named (aria-label or aria-labelledby on the aside) so it is identifiable in a landmark list; the name should not vanish at a breakpoint.
findings.basis: Standard: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 / ARIA landmark naming (an unnamed complementary region is announced as "complementary"); source: the aside has no aria-label/aria-labelledby and the only heading is the one the ≤640 rule hides. Nothing else in the panel names the region (the sheet toggle's name is the record's name, which is content, not region identity).
findings.suggestedFix: Add `aria-label="Selection details"` to the aside (it then keeps its name at every width and the visible heading can stay hidden on phones).
findings.notes: The sheet's own behaviour is otherwise correct and gated: aria-expanded on the toggle, `inert` while collapsed under 641 px (InfoPanel.tsx:360-374, 397) — which the a11y gate asserts in both readers.
